terms.gloss: pursuit, interest, activity one gives oneself to
evidence: Cic. Sen. 76: sunt pueritiae studia certa
Hor. S. 2.1.27–28: quot capitum vīvunt, totidem studiōrum mīlia
terms.comment: In the plural, the things a person likes to do, at any age.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 12.30.2: maximīs occupātiōnibus distinēbar (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The things that keep one busy; often plural.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.19: virtūtis enim laus omnis in āctiōne cōnsistit
terms.comment: Activity in general; the activity of the mind is agitātiō mentis (Cic. Off. 1.19).

terms.grammar: relative clause with agō, in the subjunctive
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.19: nīl habeō quod agam

phrases.latin: sunt pueritiae studia certa: num igitur ea dēsīderant adulēscentēs?
phrases.english: childhood has its own pursuits: do young men miss them, then?

phrases.latin: quī etiam in maximīs occupātiōnibus … dē ratiōne Latīnē loquendī accūrātissimē scrīpserit
phrases.english: who, even in the midst of his heaviest occupations, wrote with the greatest care on the method of speaking Latin

phrases.latin: nīl habeō quod agam et nōn sum piger: ūsque sequar tē
phrases.english: I’ve nothing to do and I’m not lazy: I’ll follow you all the way

sources: Lewis & Short: studium · Lewis & Short: occupatio · Lewis & Short: actio
Cicero’s De senectute, Brutus and De officiis, and Horace’s Satires, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
